document.title: Where Did The Monitor Arm Go?

turns.text: Where did the monitor arm go?

scenes.visualBeat: Three product cards appear; the third card fades out abruptly.

turns.text: We seeded three items: keyboard, dock, and arm. The local service is running, but the list looks short.

scenes.visualBeat: Terminal shows npm run demo; browser list displays only two items.

turns.text: I checked the code. The service projects the Products entity and marks it readonly. That explains why I cannot create new items.

scenes.visualBeat: Cursor hovers over @readonly annotation; a create request icon turns red.

turns.text: But readonly does not hide existing rows. I added a filter: stock greater than zero. Suddenly, the arm disappeared again.

scenes.visualBeat: Filter bar updates; monitor arm card slides away, leaving keyboard and dock.

turns.text: Wait. The arm has zero stock. The filter is doing its job. It is not a bug; it is a business rule.

scenes.visualBeat: Zoom into monitor arm card showing stock: 0; a checkmark appears.

turns.text: Remove the filter, and all three return. The service is healthy. Your data model controls what the API sees.

scenes.visualBeat: Filter removed; all three product cards reappear in the list.

turns.text: Check your filters next. This is a local prototype; production auth is separate work. Try it in your CAP project.

scenes.visualBeat: Narrator points to a local terminal prompt; text overlay notes prototype scope.

document.title: The read-only shopping trip

turns.text: Why did that create request fail?

scenes.visualBeat: Alex points at error log, Sam looks confused.

turns.text: The service explicitly marks Products with @readonly annotations.

scenes.visualBeat: Illustration of a shield blocking a write arrow.

turns.text: So we really can’t adjust stock here at all?
Exactly. The annotation deliberately rejects any create attempt.

scenes.visualBeat: Terminal shows rejected POST request turning into 405 status.

turns.text: But we still pull all inventory data normally.
Right. Queries run fine, just no actual purchases.
I was genuinely worried my shopping cart would break.

scenes.visualBeat: Terminal outputs keyboard and dock stock, ignoring zero-stock arm.

turns.text: Does this mean production blocks everything permanently now?
Not at all. That’s just a local prototype scope.

scenes.visualBeat: Illustration showing separate production deployment pipelines branching off.

turns.text: CAP projections aren’t automatically read-only anyway.
So that 405 is just our deliberate guard.
The cart stays safe.

scenes.visualBeat: Code editor highlights @readonly annotation next to entity definition.

turns.text: I’ll verify annotations before drafting my next checkout form.
And double-check if we’re testing a prototype or live system today.

scenes.visualBeat: Both developers close laptops, nodding at a clean terminal prompt.
